entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Durand of Huesca was a Spanish Waldensian who converted to Catholicism in 1207, marking a significant turning point in his life and faith.

Born in Huesca, Aragon, Spain around 1180, Durand was raised in a devout Christian family. His early life was shaped by the teachings of the Waldensian movement, a Christian sect that emphasized simplicity, poverty, and evangelism.

In 1207, Durand was baptized into the Catholic Church, a decision that would have far-reaching consequences for his family and community. This conversion not only marked a personal transformation for Durand but also had significant repercussions for the Waldensian movement, which was subsequently persecuted by the Catholic Church.

Today, Durand of Huesca is remembered as a complex figure who navigated the complexities of religious identity and loyalty during a tumultuous period in Spanish history.

His legacy serves as a reminder of the intricate web of religious and cultural influences that shaped the medieval world.
